title: Titanic · four-color ship and two masts
parts: One 269 mm Titanic: red lower hull, black upper hull, white decks, four orange funnels with black tops
Two separate orange masts laid flat; assembly required
material: PLA: red and black Bambu Basic; white and orange Clas Ohlson Universal / Generic PLA

snapshots.caption: Before start: entire textured plate viewed empty of print objects; pale prior outlines remain, plate seated.
During preparation: plate remains without model deposition, head above the bed. This is preparation evidence, not first-layer or finished-part evidence.

Paused before first layer after orange A4 assist-motor overload. No model deposition visible; pale prior outlines remain and short orange material is near the parked head/purge area. Camera cannot diagnose the spool/feed/buffer obstruction.

Hourly camera during unchanged PAUSE at layer0/319 with orange A4 feed overload: no model deposition; pale prior outlines and short orange material near parked head/purge area remain visible. Spool/feed/buffer cause still requires physical inspection.

Hourly camera during PAUSE before the first layer: no Titanic model deposition visible; pale rectangular outlines remain and toolhead is parked left. Camera does not show the AMS spool or establish the physical feed cause.

Hourly camera during unchanged PAUSE before the first layer: no model deposition visible; pale rectangular outlines remain and head parked left. AMS spool is not shown; physical feed cause remains unverified.

Camera after printer reports RUNNING with error 0 on the same accepted job: still layer 0/319 with no model deposition visible; pale rectangular outlines and left parked head remain. This does not verify extrusion, adhesion, or a physical feed repair.

First observed model deposition after the feed pause, at reported layer 5/319: red elongated hull material and orange material are visible on the plate. Toolhead obscures some areas; this confirms deposition, while complete adhesion, stability and physical feed repair remain unverified.

Hourly camera at reported layer 45/319: red hull walls and rectangular purge tower have grown, and visible bases remain on the plate. No obvious spaghetti or detached major part in this view. Toolhead partly obscures hull; full adhesion and final quality remain unverified.

Hourly camera at reported layer 80/319: black material is now visible above the red hull and on the purge tower. Visible bases remain on the plate, with no obvious detached major part or broad spaghetti in this view. Toolhead partly obscures the upper hull; full adhesion and final quality remain unverified.

Hourly camera at reported layer 108/319: black upper hull and purge tower have grown above the red lower layers. Visible bases remain on the plate with no obvious major detachment or broad spaghetti. Toolhead partly obscures the upper hull; full adhesion and final quality remain unverified.

Hourly camera at reported layer 128/319: white top material is now visible above the black/red hull and on the purge tower. Visible bases remain on the plate with no obvious major detachment or broad spaghetti. Toolhead partly obscures the upper hull; full adhesion and final quality remain unverified.

Hourly camera at reported layer 147/319: white upper hull/deck and purge tower have grown above black/red layers. Visible bases remain on the plate with no obvious major detachment or broad spaghetti in view. Toolhead partly obscures the left hull; full adhesion and final quality remain unverified.

notes: Started exactly once after current human readiness and repaired orange-feed confirmation. Exact unique-file upload/readback SHA-256 and archive MD5 verified; fresh clear-bed camera, all four live PLA colors/profiles, AMS mapping and both 0.4 mm nozzles checked. Printer LAN address had changed; direct M4 connection authenticated the configured device. Previous Enigma job was terminal and its monitor stopped; controller ownership reconciled before start. SUCCESS acceptance matches new file, MD5, plate and sequence. Independent fresh RUNNING at layer 0/319, error 0, estimated 518 minutes remaining confirms preparation, not extrusion. Initial acceptance retained old layer 73 from Enigma before resetting to 0. Retained HMS notification 0500-0200-0003-000A has unknown text and unchanged timestamp predating the completed Enigma job; classification does not establish physical resolution. No error-clearing command was sent. Exact original reviewed 269 mm four-color ship and two flat orange masts reused; no reslicing. Red A1 / black A3 / white A2 / orange A4 map [0,2,1,3] to AMS0 physical0. PVA unused. First-layer adhesion, physical quality, fine details and mast fit remain unverified. Duration and material remain estimates; actual measurements unknown. Paused before model deposition at layer0/319 with active 0700-8010 and new HMS0700-6300-0002-0001: orange A4 AMS assist motor overload. Prior human feed-fixed confirmation did not prevent recurrence. Physical spool/feed/buffer inspection is required; exact cause unknown. Fresh camera shows no model deposition and short orange material near parked head/purge area; it cannot identify feed-path obstruction. No automatic resume, error clearing, unloading/loading or replacement start authorized. At that observation the same accepted job remained paused; no reslicing justified by a physical-feed fault. At 06:02:59 UTC Oct 29, the same orange A4 overload had a new occurrence timestamp while the job remained PAUSE at layer 0/319. Nozzle measured 211 C with target 42 C, falling to 173 C by 06:03:30; the preceding intervention is unknown. No printer control commands were sent by this monitor. Physical feed inspection remains required before any authorized resume. At 08:39:10 UTC Oct 29, the same job reported RUNNING with error 0, orange A4 selected and nozzle 215 C. The monitor sent no resume or other printer control command; preceding human intervention is unknown. Still layer 0/319 and no model deposition visible in the 08:39:19 camera. First layer and physical feed repair remain unverified. Monitoring interval remains 30 minutes at human request. At 09:09:06 UTC Oct 29, printer RUNNING at layer 5/319, 5%, error 0 and estimated 491 minutes remaining. The 09:09:16 camera now shows red elongated hull material and orange deposition on the plate, confirming extrusion and progress past the first layer. The toolhead obscures some areas, so complete adhesion/stability remain unverified. No new HMS occurrence or printer command from this monitor.
